voluminous, pulsatile, highly vascularized mass in both nasal cavities

concepts.why: The presence of a highly vascularized mass in the nasal cavities, along with significantly elevated serum thyroglobulin levels and biopsy results confirming VTC metastasis, supports this diagnosis.

The combination of a hypervascular tumor in the nasal cavity, considerable uptake regarding rib and vertebral lesions on radioiodine scintigraphy, and significantly elevated serum thyroglobulin levels suggests papillary thyroid carcinoma with metastasis.

The presence of a hypervascular tumor in the nasal cavity, along with significantly elevated serum thyroglobulin levels and biopsy results confirming VTC metastasis, could also suggest follicular thyroid carcinoma with metastasis.

Although less likely, the presence of a highly vascularized mass in the nasal cavities and significantly elevated serum thyroglobulin levels could also suggest medullary thyroid carcinoma with metastasis, especially given the low iodine uptake of the sinonasal tumor.

The aggressive nature of the disease, with metastasis to the rib and vertebra, could suggest anaplastic thyroid carcinoma, although this diagnosis is less likely given the absence of specific findings indicative of anaplasia.
The hypervascular and pulsatile tumor found in the nasal cavities explains the uncovered facts of a highly vascularized mass.
